title: Young Du Moulin: refuge-trust justifies; sense-trust is perfection, often delayed
source_text: CXVIII. Eadem distinctione cum Davenantio utitur etiam, ut supra ostensum est, Petrus Molinaeus, Petri Molinaei filius Theologiae Doctor & Canonicus Cantuariensis, cujus quoque testimonio usi sumus in Thesibus, istis quas vellicat author ille, quicum jam nobis res est. Docet enim fiduciam illam, quae est causa formalis fidei justificantis, & instrumentum justificationis nostrae, esse fiduciam quam vocat perfugii, per quam ad Deum confugimus, & ipsi innitimur, Christumque amplectimur, & ei adhaeremus; non vero fiduciam, quae fiducia sensus ab eo appellatur; per quam sentimus nos Christum apprehendisse, & per eum veniam a Deo esse consecutos. Quinimo multos esse qui Christum vere apprehendunt, necdum tamen sentiunt se illum apprehendisse; & qui sunt coram Deo vere justificati, etsi de eo nondum certi & persuasi sint. Quoniam haec persuasio non pertinet ad fidei essentiam, sed solum ad ejus perfectionem; & est verae ac robustae fidei fructus & consequens quoddam.
pass_a_gloss: The same distinction with Davenant is used also, as was shown above, by Peter Du Moulin, son of Peter Du Moulin, Doctor of Theology and Canon of Canterbury, whose testimony we also used in those theses which that author who is now dealing with us plucks at. For he teaches that that trust which is the formal cause of justifying faith, and the instrument of our justification, is the trust he calls of refuge, by which we flee to God and lean on him, embrace Christ and adhere to him; not the trust he calls trust of sense, by which we feel we have apprehended Christ and through him obtained pardon from God. Indeed many truly apprehend Christ who do not yet feel they have apprehended him; and who are truly justified before God though not yet certain and persuaded of it. Because this persuasion does not belong to faith's essence, but only to its perfection; and it is a fruit and certain consequence of true and robust faith.
pass_b_english: Young Du Moulin uses Davenant's distinction: refuge-trust (fleeing to God, embracing Christ) is justifying faith's formal cause and instrument.
Sense-trust — feeling one has already grasped Christ and received pardon — is perfection, not essence; many justified believers lack it for a time.
